questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Importance of Work' refers to.
questions.a: Work is any physical or mental effort directed toward producing a good or performing a service that is useful to oneself or to others.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Importance of Work'.
questions.a: Work is purposeful effort that creates value for individuals and for society; without work no society can function.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Importance of Work' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Paid Work' refers to.
questions.a: Paid work is work for which a person receives a wage, salary, or fee in return for the goods produced or services rendered.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Paid Work'.
questions.a: Paid work is rewarded with money; the payment may be a fixed salary, a daily wage, or a fee per task.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Paid Work' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Work

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Voluntary Work' refers to.
questions.a: Voluntary work is work done willingly and without payment for the benefit of the community or a cause.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Voluntary Work'.
questions.a: Voluntary work is driven by a sense of service rather than money; examples include helping during floods or cleaning a park.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Voluntary Work' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Work

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Occupation and Profession' refers to.
questions.a: An occupation is the regular work a person does to earn a living; a profession is an occupation that requires specialised training and knowledge.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Occupation and Profession'.
questions.a: All professions are occupations, but not all occupations are professions; professions need formal training and skill.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Occupation and Profession' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Occupation and Profession

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Division of Labour' refers to.
questions.a: Division of labour is the splitting of a task into smaller parts, with different people specialising in different parts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Division of Labour'.
questions.a: Division of labour increases efficiency and quality because each worker focuses on a specialised part of the task.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Division of Labour' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Division of Labour

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Contribution of Workers to Society' refers to.
questions.a: Workers in different fields produce goods and provide services that together meet the needs of society and drive its progress.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Contribution of Workers to Society'.
questions.a: Society depends on the combined contribution of farmers, factory workers, teachers, doctors, and many others.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Contribution of Workers to Society' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Contribution of Workers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Changing Nature of Work' refers to.
questions.a: The nature of work changes over time due to new technology, new needs, and social changes, creating new occupations and reducing some old ones.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Changing Nature of Work'.
questions.a: Technology and social change create new kinds of work while making some traditional jobs less common.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Changing Nature of Work' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing Nature of Work
